notes.decision: Read as ⲉⲩⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ + ⲛ̄ϩⲙⲁϣⲉ — 'which are likened, which are fitted/measured' to him. The verb ⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ 'be like, resemble' is doubled with ϩⲙⲁϣⲉ which is obscure here but possibly related to a measuring/fitting root. The soul finds firmaments tailored to its character.

In glossary 'lust/concupiscence' (negative register), but here in positive ecclesial-paraenetic context — 'so that the catechumens may ⲗⲁⲍⲗⲉⲍ in him.' Reduplicated emotive root yields 'rejoice/exult' or 'long ardently for' in this positive-affective use. Translated 'exult' to capture the intensified affective force without the sexual connotation.

Per accumulated vocabulary, habitual/customary discourse marker. Introduces the typological case-description: 'this is it — habitually, the woman in his house...' i.e., 'this is the case: as is the custom...'

Read as ⲉⲥ- (circumstantial fem.) + ⲛ̄-ⲧⲟⲟⲧ-ϥ̄ 'at his hand.' The wife is 'at his hand' yet treated as a stranger — captures the Manichaean catechumen-motif of cohabitation without conjugal bond (in line with the Three Seals of the Elect, esp. signaculum sinus).

Lyc. compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲗⲉ (cf. ⲣ̄ⲥⲗⲟ̄ⲉ 'sojourn' in glossary; ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲗⲉ likely 'sojourn, dwell as stranger') = 'place of sojourning' = inn, lodging-place. The catechumen treats his own house as a temporary lodging — perfect Manichaean detachment.

Tentatively translated 'an early stay,' reading as Lyc. orthographic variant of ⲡϣⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'first/early/morning' substantivized with the dwelling-context. Could alternatively be a sojourn-noun. Fits the sense 'he dwells in a house [as a stranger does], for some days and some months.'

Translated 'simply' as Lyc. reflex of Greek ἁπλῶς 'simply, plainly, without distinction' — fits the construction 'reckoned before him simply as strange men.' Could alternatively read ϩⲁ-ⲡⲟ̄ 'before the face' but the simply/wholly sense fits idiomatic patterns elsewhere in the Kephalaia.

Read as qualitative of ⲗⲱⲕϩ̄/ⲗⲱϫϩ̄ in the sense 'lodge, be quartered' — captures the temporary-quartering of the catechumen's kinsmen. The defilement-sense in glossary (ⲗⲱⲭⲍ̄) seems contextually unsuitable here.

Translated as continuation of a vessel-parable from previous page: 'they treat these vessels' with ϣⲁⲩⲣⲧⲍⲉ as habitual ϣⲁⲩ + ⲣⲧⲍⲉ 'do likewise' (cf. accumulated ⲣⲧⲍⲉ). ⲛⲛⲓⲍⲛⲉⲉⲩ tentatively read as 'these vessels' (Lyc. ϩⲛⲁⲩ 'vessel,' plural form).

Read as Lyc. perfect 3sg.m 'he placed' (= ⲁϥⲕⲁ with proclitic ⲙ̄- of unclear function — possibly emphatic or conjunctional). The parallel construction with ⲁϩⲡⲱⲣⲕ (line 4) and ⲁϩⲕⲁ (line 4, 9) — all 3sg.m perfects in ⲁϩ- — supports this reading.

ⲡⲱⲣⲕ here means 'uproot, draw out' (= Sah. ⲡⲱⲣⲕ̄/ⲡⲱⲣϫ) rather than 'swear' (cf. accumulated entry: 'to swear / to draw forth'). The directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄- 'out from' demands the spatial reading: he has uprooted his reflection out of the cosmos.

Translated 'the exalted one' per accumulated vocab ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ 'be exalted/lifted up.' Refers to the catechumen elevated through the qualities listed (carefulness, toil, love). Alternative reading 'the holy one' (= ⲡⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃⲉ with scribal slip ⲧ for ⲁ) is possible but less likely given the verbal force of ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ.
Lyc. variant for ϩⲓⲥⲉ 'toil, labor' (with ⲗ for ϩ — unusual but attested in some Lyc. forms). The triplet 'carefulness + toil + love' represents the catechumen's threefold ascetic dedication.

Citation of 1 Cor 7:30 (οἱ ἀγοράζοντες ὡς μὴ κατέχοντες). Lyc. ⲧⲁⲩ likely renders 'possess/buy/acquire.' The full citation Lines 12-15 paraphrases 1 Cor 7:29-31, including 'living in this cosmos as if not in distress' (rather than 'as if not using it' from Paul's ⲉⲩⲭⲣⲱ ⲉⲣⲟϥ).

Doubled form translated 'watching, watching.' Tentative; possibly an iterative-intensive construction on a verb of seeing/watching (cf. ⲱⲣϩ̄ 'watch,' ⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲥ 'be vigilant'). The doubling-pattern matches Coptic typological iteratives (cf. accumulated ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲁⲛ 'in this same manner again'). Alternative readings include 'by company, by company' or 'how many, how many' (= ⲟⲩⲏⲣ ⲟⲩⲏⲣ). Flagged for parallel research.

Translated 'abides' — qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩⲛ 'remain, abide' (with -ⲧ qualitative ending). Construction ⲉⲣⲉ + subject + qualitative gives the durative 'while X is in a state.' Alternative readings 'is set' (qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ?) or 'is alone' (= ⲙⲁⲩⲁⲁⲧ) are less probable given context.

Read as ϫⲓ ⲙ̄ⲕⲁϩ 'take pain/wear oneself out' applied to feet — the catechumen wearies his feet going to church. ⲕⲁⲧ as Lyc. variant of ⲕⲁϩ 'pain, suffering' (with -ⲧ ending unusual but possible). The catechumen's habitual ecclesial attendance is more strenuous than care for his own house.

Translated 'which are profitable.' ϯ-ⲍⲏⲩ = ϯ-ϩⲏⲩ 'give profit, be useful' (idiomatic). Alternative reading 'which are given (as profit)' — passive of ϯ — is also possible. Both fit the catalogue of dignities (silver, gifts, honors, favors) detached from the catechumen's heart.

Translated 'being gathered' — taking ⲥⲟ̄ϩⲣ as Lycopolitan qualitative of ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather, assemble' (cf. ⲡⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲥ 'the gatherer' in glossary; ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲍ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'the Gatherer-Inward'). The catechumen during his life is gathered into the holy church — ecclesiological language of incorporation.

Translated 'who has no equal value' — Coptic idiom 'has no value with-her' = 'is without comparable price, priceless.' The pearl's incomparable worth is the point of the parable: catechumens not returning to a body are of incomparable value, like the pearl described in Mani's Treasure of Life.

Translated 'gather' — most likely Lyc reflex of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'select, choose' or ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' with 3pl object suffix. Recurs in segment 23 paired with ⲃⲱⲗ 'release' as 'release them and gather them' — confirming the 'gather/collect' sense in the harvest typology.

Translated 'she chooses (the icon), and she goes for herself' — taking ⲛ̄ⲥ̄- as 3sg.f conjunctive both times: she (Mercy) chooses (one of the many icons in which she is likened) and goes inward for her own (sake/journey) to the country of the beautiful ones. Subject of all verbs is feminine ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲉ 'mercy.'

Translated 'his progress.' The lexeme ⲫⲛⲟ recurs both as noun here and as verb in segment 25 (where it governs 'inward unto him'). Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲛ 'transfer, pass over' nominalized; or related to ⲡⲱⲛⲉ 'go forth, proceed.' The agricultural-eschatological context (release, gathering, ascent) supports a 'progress, journey, transit' sense. Tentative.

Translated as verb 'proceeds' — same root as the noun in segment 24. The going-up of the catechumen 'proceeds inward unto him' = his ascension and purification together constitute the inward-leading movement. Preserves the directional-soteriological semantics central to the Manichaean ascent doctrine.

Translated 'a remission of sins.' ⲕⲁⲛⲁⲃⲉ = ⲕⲁ-ⲛⲁⲃⲉ (causative of ⲕⲱ 'leave, remit' + ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin') — the standard Coptic noun for 'remission/forgiveness of sins,' here as the object of the catechumen's prayer asked from God and Church.

Translated 'may be gathered inward.' ⲥⲱⲩⲍ = Lyc ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' (already in glossary as ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲍ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'Gatherer-Inward'). The future-relative construction expresses the soteriological aim of the confessional prayer: that all the catechumen's works — both former and latter sins, once forgiven — be gathered up and reckoned to his honor.

Translated 'the hope which is set for us through your hand.' ⲱⲉⲕ likely a Lyc qualitative form related to ⲟⲩⲱⲏ/ⲱⲱⲕ 'set, place, dwell' — 'the hope which is established/given for us through you.' The 2sg ⲉⲕ may be relational rather than verbal.

Rendered 'even unto.' ϣⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ = ϣⲁ-ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'as far as inward' = 'even unto, right up to'; ⲁⲛ here intensive 'even.' Marks the inclusive scope of Mani's pedagogical reach: not only the Elect but even the catechumens received instruction.

Rendered 'you did not lift your hand from them.' ⲙⲡⲉⲕ-ϥⲓ-ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧⲕ ⲛⲥⲱⲩ — negated perfect of ϥⲓ-ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁ- 'remove one's hand from' = 'withdraw, abandon.' Standard idiom for not abandoning instruction.

Rendered 'with decrees.' ⲍⲛ̄- 'with' + ⲛⲉⲧⲱϣ 'commands, decrees' (from ⲱϣ 'cry out, decree'). Paired with ⲍⲙⲡⲛⲛⲏ 'in the Spirit' as the dual register of catechetical instruction: spiritual and ordinance-based.

Rendered 'shall they reach this end?' ⲁⲧⲟ likely a verb of attaining/being weighed (cf. ⲧⲟ̄ⲁⲧ 'equality/proportion' in glossary, from ⲧⲱⲧ 'be joined, equal'). The disciples' question concerns whether pre-conversion sins shall be brought to reckoning at the eschaton. Alternative: 'shall they be reckoned to this end' (judicial weighing). Either reading preserves the eschatological-juridical sense.

Left as 'the [...]' with lacuna following. ⲡⲧⲉⲉ is partial — possibly ⲡⲧⲏⲩ 'wind/spirit,' ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ 'the All,' or another idol-class term. The verb ⲥⲉⲃⲉⲥⲑⲁⲓ ('reverence') governs it. Cannot determine without parallels.
Rendered 'false witness.' ⲙⲛⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩϫ 'state-of-witness of falsehood' = false witness; standard biblical-legal sin-category in this list (idolatry/blasphemy/murder/adultery/magic/false witness).
Rendered 'set our heart at rest.' ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲛⲉ Lyc reflex of ⲙⲟⲧⲛ/ⲙⲟⲧⲛⲉ 'rest, ease' causative; standard idiom 'set the heart at rest' for receiving authoritative instruction that resolves uncertainty.

Rendered 'a great raising-up.' ⲧⲟⲛⲱ is a Lycopolitan substantival form related to ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise up' (per terminology guide must preserve vertical/exposing semantics). Here in idiomatic predicate-construction with ⲡⲓⲥⲉϫⲉ 'this saying' it functions as 'a weighty/elevated matter,' but the vertical root is preserved by 'raising-up.'

ⲡⲓⲥⲉ at end of line 1 + [ⲭ]ⲉ at start of line 2 forms ⲡⲓⲥⲉϫⲉ 'this saying' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲡⲓⲥⲉⲭⲉ in K. on lifespan-question). Lycopolitan ⲭ for ϫ. The conjunction ⲭⲉ 'that' which follows is a separate word.

Rendered 'putting-away-of-sin.' Compound: ⲕⲁ ('leave, set aside') + ⲛⲁⲃⲉ ('sin') + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('forth') = the act of laying-aside / releasing sin = confession-with-remission. Distinct from but parallel to Greek μετάνοια. Recurs in line 22 (ⲟⲩⲕⲁⲛⲁⲃⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ϩⲁ ⲛⲉϩⲙⲛⲧⲥⲉⲃⲉⲟⲩⲉ 'a putting-away-of-sin on account of his foolishnesses'). The hyphenated rendering preserves the morphology rather than substituting 'confession' or 'remission.'

Rendered 'strengthen himself' / 'establish himself firmly.' ⲧⲁⲭⲣⲟ = Lycopolitan ⲧⲁϫⲣⲟ 'be firm, strengthen' (already in glossary as ⲧⲁⲭⲣⲟ). The reflexive ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'to himself' indicates the catechumen's self-confirmation in the gift of repentance.

Rendered 'they shall release forth.' ⲕⲱ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ is the standard Coptic verb of 'forgiving/releasing' sins; the directional 'forth' is preserved per the principle of preserving spatial-directional semantics, paralleling ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release.'

Translated 'the faithful catechumens. The catechumen who...' — the apparent doubling actually marks a transition from the general topic ('the works of the faithful catechumens') to the per-individual prescription ('the catechumen who shall truly believe shall do...'). Standard Coptic discourse-pattern: general → specific.

ⲍⲉⲣⲕⲣⲁⲧⲉⲩⲉ = Greek ἐγκρατεύεσθαι 'exercise self-control'; ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ = ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϥ 'over himself' (Lyc. ϩ for ϥ). Rendered 'exercising continence over himself' to preserve the reflexive semantic. Pairs with ⲧⲉⲣⲕⲣⲁⲧⲓⲁ in line 7.

Compound ⲡⲉϩ- ('his') + ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲛ̄ⲕⲁⲧⲉ ('sleep,' = Sah. ⲛⲕⲟⲧⲕ). 'His place of sleeping' = sleeping-chamber/marriage-bed. The catechumen purifies even his sleeping-place during the Sunday observance — i.e., abstains sexually.

Direct attestation of the Manichaean signaculum oris — abstention from flesh and blood. ⲧⲏⲣϩ = ⲧⲏⲣϥ 'all/whole' (Lyc. ϩ for ϥ); ⲡⲥⲟⲛⲁϩ = ⲥⲛⲟϥ 'blood' (Lyc.). The catechumen's Sunday discipline mirrors the elect's permanent rule.

Read as variant/orthographic form of the verbal noun on ⲱⲱⲃⲉ 'transgress' (in glossary). The ⲯ-onset is unusual; possibly reflects ⲡ̄ⲱⲱⲃⲉ. Translated 'this transgression' as the contextual fit with ⲡϯⲧⲕⲉⲥ ⲛ̄ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'sting of the soul' — the moral-psychological pair the catechumen guards his hands from.

ⲭⲁ-ⲁⲛ-ϥ̄ likely 'leave/place it from him' — the catechumen 'keeps it (his prayer-routine) by his hand' through observance (παρατήρησις) over them (the prayer-hours). The construction ⲕⲱ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ usually means 'set down from one's hand' = 'cease,' but in this devotional context the sense seems opposite: actively maintain. Tentative.

ⲍⲃⲥⲱ = ϩⲃⲥⲱ 'garment' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ), NOT ⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching.' Editor's bracketed [ⲃ] secures the reading. The catechumen's good deeds are: fast performed, garment given (alms to elect), daily communion (eucharist) with the holy ones. This triad of fast/almsgiving/communion structures lines 17-19.

ⲣ̄- ('do') + ⲡⲧⲡⲉϣⲉ ('the half-share, the portion'). Verbal idiom 'take part, share in.' The catechumens 'share in his (apostolic) work for food' — i.e., they participate in the work of refining the Living Soul through proper alimentary discipline.

Structural division: the year is split into 'the half (= 50 Sundays) of obedience' (lines 3-20) and 'the other half — namely sins' (this line). ⲁⲕⲙⲏⲛ = Greek ἀκμήν 'still, namely.' The catechumen's sin-side is then quantified: a fourth-portion of merit is preserved through Church-patronage (ⲡⲁⲧⲣⲱⲛⲓⲁ) on account of his gnosis-acts (separating Light, hymning the Illuminator).

ⲥⲁⲣ-ⲟⲩ likely from ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread, divide' with 3pl object. ⲁϯⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ — translated 'into the portion of kinds' on the basis of glossary entry ⲧϯⲉ 'portion/half.' The image is forensic-mathematical: the sins are sorted into kinds, and one quarter is reserved as merit-credit through the Church's patronage.
From glossary: 'fourth/quarter.' The reserved quarter is the soteriological remainder credited to the catechumen through the Church's patronage despite the half-year of sins.

The defining gnostic act: separating Light from Darkness (cf. glossary ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'separate forth'). This is what differentiates the catechumen from the worldly: knowing the dualistic gnosis sufficient to make the cosmic distinction operative in his own life.

ⲕⲉⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ = 'the other rest' — pairing with the hymn/prayer to the Illuminator just mentioned. Either (a) a second devotional act, or (b) the eschatological rest awaiting the catechumen as result of his hymn-offering. Sense uncertain due to following lacuna.
Translated 'the days when he became a catechumen.' ⲁϩⲣ̄ is Lyc. perfect ⲁϥⲣ̄- with ϩ for ϥ; ⲣ̄- + ⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ = 'become a catechumen, enter the catechumenate.'

Tentatively rendered 'they bring them to perfection.' The element ⲝⲁⲕⲙⲉϩ is opaque; possible analyses include (a) Greek-derived verb on ἀκμάζω 'be at peak, ripen,' (b) Lyc. ⲝ for ⲣ̄- giving ⲣ̄-ⲁⲕⲙⲉϩ. The verb sits in a refining-sequence: purify (ⲕⲁⲑⲁⲣⲓⲍⲉ) → ⲝⲁⲕⲙⲉϩ → adorn (ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲏ), so a perfecting/tempering sense is contextually required.

Rendered 'unto the front of the country of the Rest.' ⲧⲉⲍⲟ = Lyc. ⲧⲉϩⲏ 'front, in front of'; ⲭⲱⲣⲁ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲡⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ 'country/region of rest' — the eschatological Land of Rest where the painted icon-souls of righteous catechumens are conveyed. Standard Manichaean cosmography of the upward conveyance of refined Light.

notes.decision: Translated 'where his heart is, his face also shall be there.' This is a Manichaean recasting of Matthew 6:21 ('where your treasure is, there will your heart be also'), substituting ⲍⲟ 'face' for the second member — the catechumen's painted icon-face will be drawn up to wherever his heart's purpose is invested. ⲡⲉϩⲉⲍⲟ = ⲡⲉϩ-ⲍⲟ 'his face' with epenthetic ⲉ.

Rendered 'turns himself aside, turning forth daily.' ⲝⲓⲃⲁⲗ likely = ϣⲓⲃⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'change forth, turn aside' (Lyc. ⲝ for ϣ); paired with ⲡⲱⲛⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ which carries the same semantic field of apostate turning. Daily backsliding describes the unstable catechumen.

Translated 'the judgment that destroys his sins shall be poured upon him.' ⲡⲍⲉⲡ 'the judgment' (in glossary), ⲧⲁⲭⲟ = ⲧⲁⲕⲟ 'destroy,' ⲡⲱⲍⲧ = ⲡⲱϩⲧ 'pour, fall.' The judgment is described as a punitive outpouring upon the apostate catechumen. Note that ⲧⲁⲭⲟ here governs 'sins' as direct object — 'judgment which destroys (the) sins' may be ambiguous between 'destroys his sins (forgives him)' or 'destroys him on account of his sins'; context (the apostate case) suggests the latter — judgment-as-destruction commensurate with sins.

Rendered 'and they shall escape forth and they shall be saved.' Two future 3pl conjunctives: ⲣ̄-ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'go/escape forth' and ⲛⲟⲩⲍⲙⲉ 'be saved' (Lyc. for ⲛⲟⲩϩⲙ̄). The plural subject is unexpected after the singular catechumen; possibly refers collectively to the saving angels/judgment-administrators, or a generic-impersonal 'they shall (cause him to) escape and be saved.'

Tentatively rendered 'they shall come to him and rest him.' ϩⲁϣⲉ unidentified — possibly Lyc. for ⲱϣⲉ 'go, come' or for ⲍⲁϣ 'hasten' (in glossary). The structure 'X to him and they rest him' demands a verb of motion-toward in the death-vision context (cf. the redeemer-figures who come at the soul's exit).

Translated 'the First Light, the wise one in the Mind.' ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ is here a title of Mani himself (the apostle/teacher) as the primal Light-emanation; ⲣⲙⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'wise/intelligent' qualifying him in respect of the Mind (first faculty). Disciples gloss their teacher in terms of the noetic faculties.
